lede: Mark's Ravens won Sunday night without Lamar Jackson, in overtime, after trailing by eight with 2:25 on the clock — the exact game Brian needed and did not get. The lead is back to four and a half. Only Monday night is left.

beats.tag: Mark · Won it with the backup
beats.text: Tyler Huntley made his first start of the season and went 24-of-32 for 201 without an interception, finishing with eleven straight completions. Down 23-15 with 2:25 left, Baltimore went 71 yards in six plays, Huntley found Devontez Walker from seven, and Derrick Henry ran in the two-point conversion to tie it. Then a 14-play, seven-minute overtime drive and a Huntley sneak. Kyle Hamilton, an Atlanta kid, intercepted the pass that ended it.

Atlanta led 23-15 after Nick Folk's fourth field goal and could not finish it. Jessie Bates III had returned a Mark Andrews fumble 36 yards for the game's first touchdown — Andrews' first lost fumble in a regular-season game since 2019 — and Drake London caught seven for 118. Michael Penix Jr. took a sack on the last Falcons drive of regulation and hurt his ribs; Tua Tagovailoa threw the overtime interception. Brian stays on ten, tied with Jon and Patrick.

beats.tag: Harrison · Second, and nothing to do
beats.text: No Harrison team played Sunday night and none plays tonight, so his three-and-a-half-point Sunday has to hold on its own. He sits on 10.5, four and a half behind Mark and half a point ahead of the three-way tie. For an owner who was seventh on Saturday, that is a good place to stand still.

beats.tag: Tonight · Jon vs Zach, the last point
beats.text: Buffalo at the Rams, and it is the only game left in the week. Los Angeles is favored at home and nobody is ruled out for them; Jon is without Josh Palmer and Ed Oliver, with D.J. Moore questionable on a 91-game streak. Jon wins and he is alone in third on eleven. Zach wins and he climbs out of the dungeon, barely.
